subject: Transportation Systems
title: Point-to-Point Rocket Travel
description: Learn Point-to-Point Rocket Travel in one minute.

hook.text: SpaceX proposed using Starship to fly passengers between cities in under an hour. New York to Tokyo in 37 minutes.

buildup.text: The rocket launches to near-orbit, coasts at 17,000 mph, and lands at a floating platform near the destination.

discovery.text: The physics works. Suborbital hops cover any point on Earth faster than any plane could ever manage.

twist.text: Passengers would endure 3G acceleration, extreme vibration, and risk levels far exceeding commercial aviation.

climax.text: No regulatory framework exists. Who certifies a rocket for human point-to-point transport? Nobody knows yet.

punchline.text: Rocket travel between cities: technically possible, practically wild.

quiz.question: What is the main regulatory challenge for point-to-point rocket travel?
options: No framework exists for certifying rockets as passenger transport
